title: feat(engine): isolate rule panics and report them as diagnostics
problem: A buggy or adversarial rule that panics would abort the entire scan.
why: One rule must never be able to take down the scanner on untrusted input.
scope: Wrap each rule invocation so a panic is caught and converted into an error diagnostic.
Mark the rule as failed and continue with the remaining rules.
guidance: Use `std::panic::catch_unwind` with `AssertUnwindSafe`; keep the panic message short.
acceptance: A deliberately panicking rule produces a diagnostic, not a crash
tests: Unit test with a panicking test rule
security: Central to robustness against hostile input and third-party rules.

title: feat(engine): add a per-rule execution budget
problem: A pathological rule can consume unbounded time.
why: Bounded rule execution keeps scans predictable and protects CI timeouts.
scope: Support an optional per-rule time budget that aborts a rule and emits a diagnostic.
guidance: Combine with panic isolation; document that the budget is best-effort.
acceptance: A slow rule is aborted with a diagnostic
Disabled by default or generous default documented
tests: Unit test with a sleeping test rule

title: feat(engine): make rule execution order independent of registration order
problem: Findings are sorted after the fact, but diagnostic order and any early-exit behavior still depend on registration order.
why: Determinism should not rely on a single final sort.
scope: Define and document an explicit execution order (by rule id) and enforce it.
guidance: Sort the rule list once before execution.

title: feat(engine): refine finding deduplication for overlapping spans
problem: Dedup relies on exact identity, so two findings for the same issue at slightly different columns are both reported.
why: Duplicate findings inflate reports and baselines.
scope: Define a documented overlap rule (same rule, same file, overlapping line range) and apply it.
guidance: Prefer keeping the earliest, most specific finding.
acceptance: Tests cover overlapping and adjacent spans
security: Never merge findings from different rules.

title: feat(engine): support path and rule suppressions from configuration
problem: Suppression is limited to disabling whole rules, with no path-scoped suppressions.
why: Teams need to accept specific findings in specific files while keeping rules active elsewhere.
scope: Add a `[suppressions]` config table with `path`, `rule`, and optional `reason`, validated at load.
guidance: Emit a suppressed count in stats and reports; never drop silently.
security: Suppressions must be auditable and never silent.

title: feat(engine): validate severity and confidence overrides with diagnostics
problem: Overrides for rules that never fire are silently ignored, hiding configuration mistakes.
why: Explicit diagnostics prevent wasted configuration effort.
scope: Warn when an override targets a disabled or nonexistent rule.
guidance: Reuse the existing rule-id validation in the CLI.

title: feat(engine): expose a rule registry introspection API
problem: Tooling (docs generation, `rules` command, validation) reaches into registry internals unevenly.
why: A small, documented introspection API stabilizes tooling and the library surface.
scope: Expose metadata iteration, lookup by category, and counts as stable methods.
acceptance: CLI and validation use only the public API

title: perf(engine): memoize derived facts on the analysis context
problem: Each rule re-visits the same AST and recomputes the same facts independently.
why: Sharing computed facts reduces duplicated work as the rule count grows.
scope: Introduce a lazily-computed, per-source fact cache on the context with interior mutability.
guidance: Keep the cache invisible to rule semantics; results must remain identical.
security: Cache must not introduce cross-file leakage of mutable state.

title: feat(engine): make the finding fingerprint strategy configurable
problem: The fingerprint always hashes rule id, file, and evidence, with no way to opt into column- or line-sensitive matching.
why: Different teams need different baseline stability trade-offs.
scope: Add a documented fingerprint strategy option (default unchanged).
guidance: Keep the default exactly as today so baselines remain valid.
security: Changing strategy invalidates baselines; document explicitly.

title: feat(engine): introduce pipeline stages and hooks
problem: The scan pipeline is a single function with no extension points, so experimentation requires forking the engine.
why: Stable stages and hooks let future analysis passes integrate without destabilizing the core.
scope: Split discovery, parsing, analysis, and post-processing into named stages with optional hooks.
guidance: Keep the public API additive; no behavior change by default.
security: Hooks must not be able to enable network or code execution implicitly.

title: feat(engine): add diagnostic codes and explicit levels
problem: Diagnostics carry only a message, making programmatic handling and suppression impossible.
why: Structured diagnostics improve tooling and user experience.
scope: Add a stable diagnostic code (for example `PARSE-001`) and level to each diagnostic; include them in JSON.
guidance: Keep messages human-readable and codes stable.

title: feat(engine): support cancellation and deadlines with partial results
problem: A long scan cannot be interrupted cleanly, and there is no overall deadline.
why: CI systems and interactive users need bounded, cancellable scans.
scope: Add an optional overall deadline and cooperative cancellation that still emits a valid partial report.
guidance: Check cancellation between files and rules; mark the report as partial.
acceptance: Deadline produces a partial report with a clear diagnostic
tests: Unit tests with a tiny deadline
security: Partial results must be clearly labeled to avoid false confidence.

title: feat(engine): add per-category findings counts to scan stats
problem: Stats expose totals by severity but not by category, limiting triage.
why: Category counts help teams prioritize which rule family to address first.
scope: Add category counts to `ScanStats` and JSON output.
acceptance: Markdown and terminal summaries may use them
